title: Comparable Analysis of the Open and Closed Forms of TRiC/CCT Chaperinin Using FOD-M Model
content: The effect of chaperonins as tools that assist the correct course of the folding process of some proteins are analysed based on the distribution of hydrophobicity in TRiC/CCT open and closed form, of which the structures are available in PDB assets. In the current analysis, chaperonins are considered as providers of the local external force field for the folding proteins. The availability of the open and closed form may shed light on the mechanism of reception of the “client” molecule (the folding protein) by transition from the open form to the closed form. That stage requires the involvement of ATP. The role of individual chains was revealed, of which the status different from other chains, i.e. capsule components, may entail a mechanism leading to the open and closed forms of chaperonin in a reversible manner. In addition, the role of the two phosducin-like protein chains present in the discussed example of chaperonin as factors introducing a peculiar polarisation within the capsule. The conclusions arising from the analysis suggest the need to treat the protein structure as the effect of compromise between the internal force field perspective (non-bonding interactions in the protein body) and optimisation considering the external force field (impact of environmental conditions).
